thread:
Jordan: FYI getting multiple escalations from CS — customers seeing a mix of 502/504 and long timeouts hitting /v1/generate. Started ~1932102000 and rate is creeping up again. opening war room. :warning:

Priya: Can you paste one of the error examples and the request IDs? need to know if this is auth, model, or gateway.

Jordan: From logs (snip):
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z gateway | request_id=req_8f1a2b status=504 upstream_timeout host=hosted-api-01 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T10:12:35Z runtime  | request_id=req_8f1a2b model=redwood-small status=200 latency_ms=12000
```
Looks like gateway timing out before runtime returns for some requests. p95 of runtime still OK but queue_depth spiked to 1200 on host.

Alex: Noted. I see the autoscaler for the gateway uses `http_concurrency` metric which currently reports active connections, but queued requests are counted elsewhere. If queue length grows, gateway doesn't scale — we hit worker saturations and the timeout is happening at the LB layer. Repro steps: run load test that simulates sustained 200 rps with batch_size=8 and long contexts (2k tokens).

Marta: Quick question — any recent deploys? I just checked deploybot: no deploys between 1932098000 and now. So config change seems more likely than code.

Sam: I can run a controlled repro in staging. Which dataset/headers do you want? and should I ramp to 200 rps?

Jordan: Yes ramp to 150->200 rps in 10m windows. Use header `X-Redwood-Test: backpressure-repro` so we can filter. Also include `X-Model: redwood-small` to reproduce kernel path.

Alex: While Sam runs repro, quick mitigations to reduce customer impact:
- reduce `gateway.max_inflight` from 500 -> 200 to throttle ingress and fail fast (less tail latency)
- flip routing fallback to `redwood-small-quant` variant for best-effort traffic
- bump dedicated pool autoscale override to +30% for next 30m
I'll prepare the commands.

Priya: Agree on mitigation. LMK when done and CS will inform affected customers with credits.

incidents-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-backpressure — follow section "emergency throttles"

Alex: Commands I ran (now):
```
kubectl -n gateway set env deploy/gateway GATEWAY_MAX_INFLIGHT=200
rtr route update --path /v1/generate --fallback-model redwood-small-quant
infra scale dedicated-pool --delta +30% --duration 30m
```

Jordan: After throttle, we saw immediate drop in 5xxs from 18% -> 3% but higher 429s for a few clients as expected. p99 latency improved from 18s -> 6s. :thumbsup:

Marta: Good. Sam — how did repro in staging go?

Sam: Ran 10m ramp to 200 rps with long contexts. Observations:
- queue_depth climbed then plateaued at ~900 when gateway.max_inflight was 500
- autoscaler evaluated `http_concurrency` and did not trigger due to misaligned metric window
- once we lowered max_inflight, queue backpressure forced upstream to return 429s quickly and runtime p50 stayed below 150ms for healthy requests
Logs attached (filtered):
```
# staging logs
gateway | time=10:22 queue_depth=912 inflight=480
autoscaler | time=10:23 metric=http_concurrency value=470 scale_decision=none
runtime | time=10:24 processed=432 latency_p50=120 p95=350 p99=1500
```

Priya: CS update: issued proactive message to 8 customers, applied $0. credit to those with >=3x failures. Waiting on confirmation from three larger customers.

Jordan: Root cause hypothesis: gateway ingress allowed too many in-flight requests while autoscaler used active connection metric. When queue backed up (long contexts, large batches), gateway timed out rather than autoscaler scaling. Two contributing factors: metric mismatch in autoscaler and gateway `max_inflight` default too high for current instance flavor.

Marta: Temporary fixes applied. Next steps we should track in follow-up tasks.

Sam: Action items I propose (assign owners inline):
- [ ] (Alex) Change autoscaler to use `queued_requests_rate` + add short-window spike detector (1m).
- [ ] (Marta) Reduce gateway default `max_inflight` for hosted pool types; rollout config to canaries today.
- [ ] (Priya/CS) Confirm impacted customers list and finalize credits communication (by EOD).
- [ ] (Jordan) Add a circuit-breaker that returns 429s earlier when queue_depth > threshold.
- [ ] (Alex) Add dashboard: queue_depth, queued_rate, inflight, p99 latency, and an alert if queued_rate > 200 for 2m.
- [ ] (Sam) Reproduce post-fixes in staging and validate no degradation for short-context traffic.

Alex: I'll open the infra PR for autoscaler change and add unit tests. ETA: 2 business days.

Marta: I'll stage the gateway `max_inflight` change in canary (50% of hosts) and monitor for regressions. ETA: today + 4 hours.

Priya: CS will follow up with the three customers and send final note once credits applied. ETA: 6 hours.

Jordan: Temporary mitigation timeline: throttles in place now, remove after autoscaler fix and canary validated. Keep war room open until canary stable or 6 hours.

incidents-bot: Assigned incident #INC-2026-317 to Jordan, priority P2.

Sam: Quick repro note for engineers — use this k6 script header to reproduce long-context workloads: `--header "X-Model: redwood-small" --batch 8 --context 2000`

Marta: Postmortem owners: Alex (infra fix), Marta (gateway config rollout), Sam (staging validation), Priya (customer communications). I'll create the postmortem doc and link it here.

Jordan: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after canary run. Leaving notes: do not change model kernels or runtime weights during canary window to avoid confounding factors. :eyes:

cs-bot: Notified customers: 8 recipients — initial message sent. Ticket IDs: CS-8342, CS-8346, CS-8351.

Priya: I'll post the final customer note in #customer-success once credits are confirmed.

Jordan: Closing war room for now — will reopen if alerts fire during canary. updating incident timeline in pager. Good job on quick mitigation. :raised_hands:
